saml2.title: SAML 2.0 identity provider
saml2.intro: The Web Browser SSO profile, all four bindings, and Single Logout. This page holds nothing: every row is an entry in ou=applications.
saml2.perSp: Every service provider gets its own metadata document. The identity provider names itself differently to each one and publishes endpoints scoped to it, which is what Okta and Ping do. In development it is minted for anything asked for — a service provider does not have to appear here before it can be pointed at this service, because asking for its metadata is what creates it. In product it is not: a name that is not registered below is a 404 at every per-service-provider path. The unscoped document at
common.unscopedAfter: works too and names one identity provider for everybody.
common.linkApplications: these entries on the applications page
saml2.noneYet: {filtered, select, yes {No service provider has used this profile yet under that filter.} other {No service provider has used this profile yet.}}
saml2.registerIntro: Optional in development, where an entityID is accepted whether or not it is here and what this buys is a metadata document to hand somebody before they have sent anything. In product it is how a service provider comes to exist: its metadata and endpoints answer only once it is registered.
saml2.registerNote: The same thing a request or a metadata fetch would do.
saml2.hMdqImport: Import one from the Metadata Query responder
saml2.mdqIntro: Asks saml2.mdqBaseUrl for the entity by name (<base>/entities/<entityID>), creates the entry if the answer describes it, and consumes the document — held to the realm's metadata trust anchors when it has any. A request from a service provider with no metadata starts the same lookup in the background. In product mode the answer must verify against a trust anchor (saml2.metadataTrustAnchors): with none, this import is refused unless saml2.mdqImportWithoutAnchors is on — and then the document is consumed with no signature check — and a lookup a request starts for an unknown entityID is not made at all.
saml2.refusedIntro: EntityIDs a request asked to be registered through the responder and was not (product mode): no trust anchor, so nothing was fetched, or an answer that did not verify against one. Newest first; this process's record, since it started. To register one, import it above or register it by hand.
saml2.shape: These decide the SHAPE of an assertion — who issued it, how long it is good for, what is signed.
saml2.shapeAfter: is the page that changes what one CONTAINS, and its SAML 2.0 set reaches this profile through the same assertion builder that serves WS-Trust and WS-Federation.
detail2.rowIdpWhy: The realm's one issuer, its OAuth issuer, the same for every service provider and every protocol (#523). The ENDPOINTS below are this service provider's own.
detail2.rowMetadataWhy: Signed, and served no-store, as every document carrying a key is: the signing key can rotate (and is regenerated on every start in development mode). This is the URL to configure the service provider from.
detail2.rowSsoWhy: HTTP Redirect, HTTP POST and HTTP POST SimpleSign. Which binding the RESPONSE comes back on is the AuthnRequest's own ProtocolBinding.
detail2.rowSloWhy: A LogoutRequest arriving from this service provider, and a bare GET to start one from here.
detail2.rowArsWhy: SOAP over HTTP, and a back channel: the browser never touches it. An artifact resolves exactly once.
detail2.entryIs: A SAML 2.0 service provider. Its entry is
common.notInRegistry: NOT in the registry yet — this page is showing what it WOULD be given
common.hEndpoints: The endpoints it is configured from
detail2.slugDigest: , which is a digest of the entityID because the entityID is not safe in a URL path segment. The percent-encoded entityID works in the same place
detail2.nameIdFormatsNone: none — it has never named one, so it gets saml2.nameIdFormat
detail2.verifiedNote: — VERIFIED against the registered signing certificates below, never against the one a request carries. no-certificate means it was signed and nothing is registered to check it against.
detail2.signedRequiredWhy: . An unsigned AuthnRequest or LogoutRequest is refused when this is yes; a signature that does not verify is refused always.
detail2.logoutNote: A <samlp:LogoutRequest> carries no return address — only SP metadata does. The SingleLogoutService endpoints of its CONSUMED metadata (below) are used first; with none, what is declared here; then saml2.defaultSingleLogoutService; and then the assertion consumer service URL this service provider last used, which is a guess and is logged as one. Consuming its metadata, or declaring an address here, removes the guess.
detail2.nothingDeclared: Nothing is declared, so the fallback above applies
detail2.addNote: Writes samlSingleLogoutService on the entry. An ldapmodify of the same attribute does exactly this.
detail2.itsRegistryEntry: its registry entry, with every attribute
certs.title: Its signing certificates
certs.intro: What this service provider's AuthnRequests, LogoutRequests and LogoutResponses are VERIFIED against, in every mode — a signature that verifies against none of them is refused. Written by consuming its metadata, by the form below, or by confirming an observed certificate. The certificate a request carries in its ds:KeyInfo is never trusted by arriving: it is shown as OBSERVED until you confirm it. RSA certificates only, because the verifier here is RSA.
certs.noneRegistered: None registered, so a signed request from this service provider is recorded as no-certificate and not verified.
certs.replaceNote: The list becomes this one certificate; empty clears it.
certs.observed: The last signed request carried this certificate, and it is not registered. It verifies nothing. Development mode encrypts an assertion to it when nothing else is on the entry; product does not. Confirm it only if it is genuinely this service provider's.
certs.noneObserved: No request has carried a certificate that is not already registered.
meta.expired: Every request from this service provider is REFUSED until a newer document is consumed.
meta.validUntilEnforced: — enforced: past it this service provider's requests are refused
meta.notRefreshable: not possible: the document was uploaded, and a stale one keeps working until its validUntil
meta.encryptedWantedWhy: — true when the document publishes a use="encryption" key; the assertion is then encrypted to it in every mode
meta.nameIdPolicy: — a NameIDPolicy asking for another is answered InvalidNameIDPolicy
meta.nameIdAny: none declared — any format asked for is answered
meta.noneConsumed: No metadata has been consumed for this service provider, so its return addresses and signing certificates are whatever was recorded or declared above.
meta.title: Its metadata
meta.intro: Consuming a service provider's metadata REGISTERS what it says: its AssertionConsumerService endpoints (a request is answered only at one of them, in every mode), its SingleLogoutService endpoints, its signing certificates, its encryption certificate, its NameIDFormats, AuthnRequestsSigned and WantAssertionsSigned. It happens only when you refresh the URL on
meta.introAfter: or upload a document here — never while somebody is signing in.
meta.consumeNote: Its entityID must be this service provider's. Nothing changes if it is refused.
meta.refreshFrom: From its samlSpMetadataUrl, or — with none —
meta.fromMdqUnset: from the MDQ responder (saml2.mdqBaseUrl, not set here)
meta.hSigningCert: The certificate its metadata must be signed with
meta.signingSet: Set: a document that is unsigned, or not signed with this key or a realm trust anchor, is refused.
meta.signingAnchors: Not set on the entry, and this realm has {n} metadata trust anchor(s) (saml2.metadataTrustAnchors): a document that verifies against none of them is refused.
meta.signingNone: Not set, and no realm trust anchor: a signed document is consumed and recorded as signed-not-verified, and the trust act is your choice of URL or document.
saml11.noProfiles: none — it has only ever been handed a 1.1 assertion through another door
saml11.title: SAML 1.1 identity provider
saml11.intro: Both browser profiles, and the SAML responder behind one of them. This page holds nothing: every row is an entry in ou=applications.
saml11.noRequest: SAML 1.1 has no request message, which is where most of the differences from
saml11.noRequestAfter: come from. A relying party cannot identify itself in the protocol, so it is named by Shibboleth's providerId parameter, by the path segment of a scoped endpoint, or it is GUESSED from the origin of the TARGET. There is also no Single Logout to configure — it arrived with SAML 2.0 — and no request signature to record.
saml11.perRp: Every relying party gets its own metadata document, minted for anything asked for, exactly as the 2.0 profile does. It is a SAML 2.0 metadata document describing a SAML 1.1 identity provider, which is what every relying party actually consumes: SAML 1.1 never had a metadata specification. The unscoped document at
saml11.noneYet: {filtered, select, yes {No relying party has taken a SAML 1.1 assertion yet under that filter.} other {No relying party has taken a SAML 1.1 assertion yet.}}
saml11.registerIntro: Optional, and it changes nothing about whether a flow is accepted — any identifier is accepted whether or not it is here. What it buys is a metadata document to hand somebody before they have sent anything, and a name to use in providerId so that nothing has to be guessed.
saml11.registerNote: The same thing a flow or a metadata fetch would do.
saml11.shape: These decide the SHAPE of an assertion.
saml11.shapeAfter: is the page that changes what one CONTAINS, and its SAML 1.1 set reaches this profile through the same assertion builder that serves WS-Trust and WS-Federation.
detail11.rowIdpWhy: The realm's one issuer, its OAuth issuer, the same for every relying party and every protocol (#523) — and so every artifact carries the same SourceID, a hash of this value. The ENDPOINTS below are this relying party's own.
detail11.rowMetadataWhy: Signed, and served no-store because the signing key is regenerated on every start. This is the URL to configure the relying party from. It carries an IDPSSODescriptor for the browser profiles AND an AttributeAuthorityDescriptor for the responder, because a Shibboleth service provider looks for its attribute authority in the second.
detail11.rowTransferWhy: Where a browser is sent to be signed in. SAML 1.1's name for what SAML 2.0 calls the Single Sign-On service. Send TARGET, and shire for where the assertion goes.
detail11.rowResponderWhy: SOAP over HTTP POST, and a back channel: the browser never touches it. It resolves artifacts (once each), returns assertions by AssertionID, and answers AttributeQuery and AuthenticationQuery — which is SAML 1.1's attribute authority.
detail11.entryIs: A SAML 1.1 relying party. Its entry is
detail11.guessed: This identifier is a bare origin, which is what this service writes down when nobody told it the relying party's name. SAML 1.1 has no request message, so a flow that sent no providerId and used no scoped endpoint leaves the audience to be guessed from the origin of the TARGET. The assertion is issued to THIS string, so a relying party expecting a different audience refuses it inside a signature check with nothing saying why. Send providerId, or use the scoped endpoint above, to make it exact.
detail11.slugDigest: , which is a digest of the identifier because the identifier is not safe in a URL path segment. The percent-encoded identifier works in the same place
detail11.sameSlugAfter: uses for this application, deliberately: one application has one handle, or the console would show one entry as two.
detail11.shire: — the shire parameter. In product mode it must be one of the samlAssertionConsumerService values on this entry, compared exactly; development records and accepts any.
detail11.noProfiles: none — it has only ever been handed a 1.1 assertion through WS-Federation or WS-Trust
detail11.nameIdFormatsNone: none — and in this protocol that is the ordinary case, because there is no NameIDPolicy to ask in. It gets saml11.nameIdFormat unless the non-spec format parameter says otherwise.
detail11.hNotHere: What is NOT here, and why
detail11.notHere: The SAML 2.0 page has rows this one does not, and none of them is missing work. No logout return address: SAML 1.1 has no Single Logout, so there is nothing to send anywhere. No request signature on the browser side: the inter-site transfer service takes no request message, so nothing there is signed. The relying party's samlSigningCertificate still matters, at the SOAP responder: it authenticates the caller of an artifact resolution or a query, by a signed <samlp:Request> or that certificate at the TLS handshake. No response binding asked for in the protocol: which of the two browser profiles is used is chosen by the non-spec profile parameter, else the binding registered for the shire on this entry (samlAcsEndpoint, from consumed metadata), else saml11.defaultProfile.
detail11.mockRpAfter: will run either profile against this service and show every check.
